What fits here →

cooling.h: Almost all the power ends as heat
cooling.p: Servers turn electricity into heat. With cooling and losses, a 20 MW data centre has about 28–31 MW of heat to get rid of, all the time.
A closed loop carries the heat to coils outside; fans blow air across them. No water, but they need the most space: 28 units for this size.
texts: fans pull air over the coil

cooling.p: Warm water falls through the tower and part of it evaporates, which carries the heat away. Smaller and fewer, but it uses water, sends blowdown to the sewer and needs Legionella testing.
Dry most of the year. On hot days water is sprayed on the incoming air. In Edmonton that is about 10.4% of the year (914 hours above 18 °C).
texts: hot day: water sprayed on the inlet air
Hours with water on, Edmonton (typical year)

cooling.h: How much room each one takes
cooling.p: Units for 20 MW, with one spare. Area is the units alone; clearances add more.
titles: Dry coolers: 806 m² of units — 28 units
Hybrid coolers: 1,613 m² of units — 48 units
Cooling towers: 220 m² of units — 7 cells

cooling.h: How much water each one uses
cooling.p: Evaporated on site in a year, at most. Dry coolers use none; towers evaporate up to 1.5 L per kWh of heat.

heat.p: Air cooling leaves heat at 25–35 °C, too cool for most heating. Liquid cooling to the chip catches 48–75% of it in water.
titles: Caught in liquid: 48–75 % of server heat
Left in the air: 25–52 % of server heat

heat.h: Lifting it with a heat pump
heat.p: A heat pump raises it to about 70 °C for a network. Each unit of electricity gives 3–4.5 units of heat.
About 65–118 GWh a year, the space and water heating of 2,222–4,051 homes in Edmonton. Offered is not used: the buildings still have to take it.
6 buildings that could take heat, by kind. Distance and price decide which are worth a pipe.

energy.p: About 28–31 MW at the meter on average, 147–163 GWh a year. The grid sees it as a steady load.
The same load carries about 19 times the carbon on Alberta's grid as on BC's.
Alberta's interim limit of 1,200 MW for new large loads is fully allocated; large data centres may bring their own generation.

water.p: Only evaporative cooling uses water on site: it evaporates in the tower, and the salts left behind are flushed to the sewer as blowdown.
At this size, at most. Dry coolers: none.
About 3,609 m³ falls on 10,676 m² of roof in a year. Set against a tower's use, it is 1%.
titles: Rain on the roof: 3,609 m³ a year

water.p: Edmonton's water is about 178 mg/L hard, Vancouver's about 20. Harder water means more blowdown for the same heat.

people.p: Fans and pumps make a steady sound. It drops about 6 dB each time the distance doubles, over open ground without walls.
About 31 units together (an assumption). The night limit of 50 dBA is reached at 249–786 m, low-noise to standard units.

materials.p: The building lasts decades; the servers are replaced every five to six years. Each refresh is a truckload of equipment out and in.
About 33,333 servers at this size (about 600 W each): 708–877 tonnes each time.
titles: Copper in the facility: 400–800 tonnes — industry figure
